originality.rationale: The full same-object 2026 determinant paper and accessible primary Cantor frame literature were compared by statement and implication. The new theorem determines every diagonal of the weighted inverse Gram and the exact inverse spectral moment; these are not entailed by the scalar determinant alone, and no checked paper states the weighted A-optimality and local variance result. The prior all-depth determinant and its frequency maximizers are credited. Priority remains conditional on incomplete global bibliography.

No independent bibliographic priority audit was conducted. Search absence alone is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a spatially resolved inverse information invariant for every cell in an exponentially growing natural Fourier sampling family, beyond determinant or spectral conditioning bounds. It solves joint product-mass and integer frequency selection for both A-optimal average and worst-coordinate noise at all depths and strengthens the exponent of odd-base finite-stage instability. The precise local variance is relevant to reconstruction error allocation, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
